# Tractor

> Tractor runs and steers Attractor-compatible agent pipelines. This repository is both a Codex plugin and a Claude Code plugin, sharing one set of skills and one MCP server configuration between them, with a deferred stdio MCP tool surface.

Repository: https://github.com/tylergannon/tractor

## Requirements

- Codex with plugin marketplace support, or Claude Code with plugin support.
- Go 1.26 or newer on the machine running the plugin.
- The Go binary install directory on the `PATH` inherited by the agent host.

## Install in Codex

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tylergannon/tractor/main/scripts/install.sh | sh
```

The script runs `go install github.com/tylergannon/tractor/cmd/tractor@latest`
and then invokes `tractor plugin install`. The latter refreshes the marketplace,
replaces the installed plugin and its cache, retires superseded MCP servers that
declare detached-run support, and removes the obsolete source-building wrapper
cache. It does not stop detached runs, and it preserves legacy MCP servers that
still own child runs. Start a new Codex task after installation or update so the
plugin's MCP server is loaded.

## Install in Claude Code

```sh
go install github.com/tylergannon/tractor/cmd/tractor@latest
claude plugin marketplace add tylergannon/tractor
claude plugin install tractor@tractor
```

Or, from inside an interactive session: `/plugin marketplace add
tylergannon/tractor` then `/plugin install tractor@tractor`. Claude Code
auto-discovers the plugin's skill from `skills/` and its MCP server from
`.mcp.json` at the repository root — the same files the Codex plugin uses, not
a separate copy. Start a new Claude Code session after installation or update,
and run `claude plugin update tractor@tractor` to pick up a later release.

## MCP server

The plugin runs the installed binary as `tractor mcp` and speaks MCP over stdin
and stdout.

The server uses `github.com/mark3labs/mcp-go`. All tools are deferred, so their definitions are loaded only when Codex needs them. Pipeline arguments are file paths rather than embedded graph schemas.

## Tools

- `validate_pipeline`: validate a JSON, YAML, or YML pipeline file.
- `start_run`: start or resume a validated pipeline and return its run ID, process ID, and log paths.
- `get_run_status`: inspect a run by run ID.
- `steer_run`: send text to the run's active steerable turn; when none is active it returns `accepted: false` and HTTP status 409.
- `stop_run`: request that a run stop; repeating the call after the graceful window escalates to a forced stop.
- `get_pipeline_schema`: return Tractor's current graph JSON Schema on demand.

`validate_pipeline` accepts `pipeline_path` and an optional `workdir`. `start_run` also accepts an optional `logs_root` and `resume`. A new run requires an empty or absent `logs_root`; use `resume: true` to continue from an existing run directory. Later operations use the `run_id` returned by `start_run`.

Each run is a detached Tractor process with atomic state under
`~/.local/state/tractor/mcp-runs`. It survives MCP and Codex restarts. A later
MCP session can inspect, steer, or stop it with the original `run_id`.

## Schema synchronization

`get_pipeline_schema` returns `graph.Graph{}.Schema()` directly. Validation and execution call Tractor's existing parser and runtime validator. The plugin does not maintain a second copy of the graph schema.

## Direct stdio use

From an installed Tractor binary:

```sh
tractor mcp
```

The command reserves stdout for MCP protocol messages. Run output and diagnostics are written to the run paths returned by `start_run`.
